interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and `subscribe_events` only hands out clones of that same channel (handle.rs:254-259). A send that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run op.tick() (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages, and cannot answer any Command - including the append_notify Timeout that drain_notifiers would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint documented at handle.rs:114-137). The crate's sibling egress paths avoid this with try_send (drain_outgoing_buf; push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs), and its own regression test states the invariant for the outgoing channel. Node-local support - the same execution also carries it: events 3,4 `unconsumed_event_bound_reached` {nodes_full:3, nodes:3, event_capacity:64}, `actor_parked` {node:1, samples_without_reply:10, reply_budget_ms:200, permanently_parked:true} and `append_notify_endpoint_withheld` {node:1, per_call_deadline_ms:300, actor_timeout_ms:1500, outer_wait_ms:4000, resolved:false}, against control events 0,1 `control_actors_responsive` {nodes_answering:3} and `control_append_notify` {origin:1, succeeded:true, idx:2}. Cluster-level consequence - execution 76557a280cf8429d8ce3102d7565decb (experiment 2b18b51118e04d8a9f0ca6001d18eb51-experiment, exit 0, all three tests passed): in a 3-node cluster where only node 1 consumes its event stream (event_capacity 8), event 2 `parked_majority_cluster` records nodes_parked:2, healthy_node_responsive:true, append_notify_timeout_reached:true, decided_before:7, decided_after:7, i.e. two of three nodes parked on unconsumed event streams and the healthy third node could not complete a write - it reached the documented Timeout endpoint for a 300ms per-call deadline and its decided index did not move across the attempt - while events 0,1 in the same run (`control_actors_responsive` {nodes_answering:3}, `control_append_notify` {origin:1, succeeded:true, idx:2}) and events 3,4 (`unconsumed_event_bound_reached`, `actor_parked` {node:2, permanently_parked:true}) show the control and the node-local freeze respectively. The comparison therefore holds at both scopes: with unconsumed bounded event streams the actor loops park, the parked node loses every command endpoint (even the documented failure), and when enough nodes park the cluster stops deciding while every node process is still alive; with the same capacity and activity and a draining consumer nothing freezes. Scope of the defect asserted: a node whose client does not consume its event stream stops participating (no ticks, no message handling, no command replies) once it has observed event_capacity transitions, for any finite capacity; the probe reaches the bound at 64 (node-local cases) and 8 (cluster case) to stay inside bounded windows, and the mechanism is capacity-independent because the send awaits whenever the channel holds capacity events. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the trigger is client-side usage and no snapshot source states a drain obligation, so the finding rests on the handle-method contract (every Command reply, and the documented Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths; (b) a dropped receiver unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as a live receiver exists; (c) the bounds witnessed are 64 and 8, not the default 1024, and no rate claim is made about how fast a deployment reaches them; (d) the cluster case parks two of three nodes in one schedule - it does not establish how many nodes a given schedule parks, only that the healthy remainder cannot decide.
limitations: The bounds witnessed are event_capacity 64 (node-local cases) and 8 (cluster case); capacity-independence and reachability at the default 1024 are argued from source, not observed.

interpretations.rationale: Current account (source-only, no receipt yet): the blocking behavior itself is settled by source - detect_and_emit_events publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` (omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited in the tick arm of the only actor loop (actor.rs:665-711); the event channel is bounded (RuntimeConfig::event_capacity, handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74) and subscribe_events hands out a shared receiver clone (handle.rs:254-259). With a live-but-unread receiver the send is Pending and the actor task parks, so op.tick() (which drives leader-election heartbeats, message resends and batch flushes), handle_incoming and command handling all stop; a caller then cannot even obtain the documented append_notify failure endpoint, because the Timeout is produced by drain_notifiers on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract at handle.rs:114-137). Sibling paths of the same actor were built to avoid exactly this (try_send + buffering in drain_outgoing_buf, actor.rs:232-258; try_send + defer in push_to_all_subs, actor.rs:301-333), and the crate's own regression test asserts the invariant for the outgoing channel ('must still be responsive... if flush_outgoing blocked on a full channel, this would hang', tests/async_runtime_test.rs:1040-1082). What is NOT yet established: an actual execution showing the parked loop and its consequence. A first local construction of the probe (draft/assurance_generated.rs: 3-node in-process cluster, event_capacity=1, subscribe_events() receiver retained and never read) compiled and ran, but the harness as written did not reach the expected state - no node blocked within 500ms, and even the drained-events control cluster had not decided an entry within the probe's 300ms append_notify deadline, so the cluster had presumably not yet progressed to a second observed transition/two-state leader view. Until the probe is repaired and executed through the controller, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified. Counter-limitations to carry: (a) the trigger is client-side usage (a retained but unread receiver) - the runtime documents no drain obligation, and event_capacity only delays the parking, it does not bound it; (b) a receiver that is dropped unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as the receiver is held; (c) no source in the snapshot states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel, so the finding rests on the contract of the handle methods (every Command-reply method, including append_notify's Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths.

Current account. Settled by source: every transition the actor observes is published with an awaited send on a channel created once in spawn_actor as async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) (handle.rs:295-323, capacity field handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74); detect_and_emit_events issues those sends (actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited from inside the tick arm of the single run select loop (actor.rs:665-711), so a Pending send there stops op.tick(), incoming handling, command handling and decided-subscriber pushes. subscribe_events hands out a clone of that same receiver (handle.rs:254-259), and append_notify's Timeout endpoint is produced by drain_notifiers on the same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract handle.rs:114-137), so a parked actor would also withhold that documented failure. NOT settled: whether an unread receiver actually parks the actor. Local construction (native feedback, not retained receipts; harness draft/assurance_generated.rs) produced two contradicting observations on the same cluster shape (3 nodes, in-process transport, event_capacity=1, tick_period=2ms): (A) with no consumer task at all, i.e. only the receiver the handle itself holds, no node reached a stable leader within 10s and every current_leader() poll timed out - consistent with the park; (B) with a per-node consumer task that reads events during a healthy phase (leader elected, entries decided, all commands answered) and then stops reading while keeping the receiver (instrumented: the task confirmed it had stopped reading), the cluster went on deciding all 24 further proposals and every node kept answering commands, and a later append_notify succeeded - inconsistent with the park. Because both variants leave an unread receiver on a bounded channel, (B) defeats the currently stated premise that 'unread receiver + capacity reached => sender stays Pending'. Possible explanations not yet distinguished: the tick arm's send may not be the blocking point in (B) (e.g. produces no further events, or the send resolves immediately because the channel is closed/space exists), or (A)'s no-progress has a different cause than the one claimed. Until the decisive channel-state observation is made, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified, so no defect is asserted. Counter-limitations to carry: a dropped receiver would unblock the actor (the send error is ignored), capacity only delays the parking, no snapshot source states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel (the finding would rest on the handle-method contract plus the deliberate try_send design of the sibling egress paths), and the event_capacity=1 configuration is an extreme point of a knob whose default is 1024.
limitations: Local construction observations (harness drafts run by the agent, not controller receipts) cannot support a formal conclusion; variant (B) also used an agent-defined tokio-backed AsyncRuntime implementation rather than the crate's TokioRuntime feature.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account of the new question, no execution yet. A follower replies to each AcceptDecide/AcceptStopSign with an Accepted that carries only the receipt's ballot and the follower's accepted_idx (follower.rs:160-175), and the leader turns those receipts into a decision when `is_chosen` sees a quorum of advertised accepted indexes (leader.rs:316-345). Both roles have a periodic callback - SequencePaxos::resend_message_timeout dispatches to resend_messages_leader/resend_messages_follower every resend_message_tick_timeout logical ticks (mod.rs:229-246) - but in the accept phase the leader's version only resends a pending StopSign (or its decide) and re-Prepares peers that are not promised (leader.rs:371-403), and the follower's version is the empty `Phase::Accept => ()` arm (follower.rs:240-269); the follower's other periodic path, flush_batch_follower, replies only when the batch flush itself advanced the accepted index (follower.rs:284-290). So the direction follower->leader has no timer-driven retry, and the leader has no way to ask a follower for its accepted index; the only later trigger is a new AcceptDecide arriving for new entries, which makes the follower advertise a (possibly larger) accepted_idx. Whether that leaves a genuinely quorum-accepted entry undecided for an unbounded interval with no enabled repair under normal (no further proposal) conditions is exactly what the registered discriminator is to decide; no defect is claimed before it runs.
limitations: The claim depends on the environment being permitted to lose a single message while the transport keeps the rest in order; the probe must drop only the Accepted reply and keep delivering everything else.

A retry of the client's own proposal (in the runtime layer) can repair the earlier entry as a side effect, so any later assertion must be scoped to 'no further proposal is made', which the core API does not itself require of a caller.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, corrected by the executed run. The suspicion was that a lost follower Accepted reply is never repaired by any timer-driven or self-initiated action, so a quorum-accepted entry stays undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives (source reading: resend_messages_leader's Accept arm only re-Prepares unpremised peers and resends a pending StopSign; resend_messages_follower's Accept arm is empty; flush_batch_follower replies only when the flush itself advanced the accepted index). Execution 9a8b2864badf41a183a56bcfe91e49a2 (experiment 34c476dd304f48f59580ab2799b029d3-experiment, exit 101) ran the probe and defeats that suspicion in the probed configuration: parsed event 1 `lost_accepted_window` records dropped=Accepted:1, follower_accepted_idx=1, accept_decide_total=1 (so no new client proposal was made in the whole 500-step window) and yet leader_decided_idx=1 with follower_decided_idx=1 - the entry did become decided. The same event names the wire traffic that did it: produced = BLE:676,Prepare:4,Promise:6,AcceptSync:6,AcceptDecide:1,Accepted:3,PrepareReq:2,Decide:1. Three Accepted replies were produced although only one AcceptDecide exists, which matches the accept-sync path in the follower: handle_acceptsync pushes a fresh Accepted carrying the follower's current accepted index (follower.rs:53-79) and it runs whenever the follower is back in Phase::Prepare, i.e. after a new Prepare/Promise cycle (Prepare:4, Promise:6, AcceptSync:6). So the acceptance is re-advertised through ballot-change and re-sync paths rather than through the empty Accept-phase resend arms; the source reading of the empty arms is unchanged, but it does not imply non-repair. Counter-limitation and necessary gap that the correction does not remove: the churn in this run may be an artifact of the previous harness's cadence (it ticked both nodes before draining and delivering anything, which can put a heartbeat reply into a later BLE round than the request that asked for it), so this receipt does not establish whether a lost Accepted is repaired when no ballot change occurs; the revised experiment measures the same window again with per-node tick-and-deliver cadence and with after_drop tracing, which will either show the entry undecided (suspicion survives in the faithful configuration) or name the repairing message. A second, independent defect in the previous harness also shows in parsed event 0 `delivered_accepted_decides` (steps_until_decided=6, leader_decided_idx=1, follower_decided_idx=0): the control read the follower's decided index before its Decide had been delivered, so that failure is attributed to the probe, not to the target. No defect is claimed for this question.
limitations: The refuting witness is a run whose protocol-level churn may have been provoked by the harness's own cadence; whether a lost Accepted is repaired without any ballot change is a necessary open gap.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. With the harness cadence corrected (one node ticked, drained and delivered at a time, so heartbeat replies land in the round that asked for them), the suspicion holds and the earlier apparent refutation is explained as an artifact of the old cadence. Execution 092538c6a04e456e8c0277f748a174d9 (experiment 9d31a7bf98034ecaa9c70e2cef669b8c-experiment, exit 0, both selected tests passed) parsed three events. Event 1 `lost_accepted_window`: steps 500, resend_periods 100, dropped Accepted:1, produced BLE:675,Prepare:1,Promise:1,AcceptSync:1,Accepted:2,AcceptDecide:1, after_drop BLE:667, accept_decide_total 1, leader_decided_idx 0, follower_decided_idx 0, follower_accepted_idx 1, follower_holds_undecided_entry true, leader_still_stable true - i.e. exactly one client proposal, no ballot change, no protocol message at all after the deliberate drop beyond heartbeats, and the entry still undecided after 100 resend periods even though the follower holds it and the leader is stable. Event 0 `delivered_accepted_decides` is the control: the same setup with the receipt delivered decides in 1 step (leader and follower both at 1), so the non-decision is attributable to the lost receipt, not to the window or to the configuration. Event 2 `later_proposal_repairs`: a second proposal decides both entries within 1 step (leader_decided_idx 2), which names the only enabled repair in that interval; the follower's decided index reads 0 there because the loop stopped as soon as the leader decided and the Decide had not been delivered yet (a probe-side reading, not a target behavior). Source support for the responsibility: the library exposes resend_message_tick_timeout, documented as 'the number of calls to tick() before a message is considered dropped and thus resent', and this snapshot's own runtime layer deliberately discards outgoing messages when its buffer exceeds the cap, documenting that as safe 'because OmniPaxos already tolerates lost messages via its own resend/retry mechanisms' (omnipaxos_runtime/src/handle.rs:52-58). In the accept phase that premise does not hold: the follower->leader direction has no retry at all, so the leader's quorum count stays one short of quorum until unrelated traffic or a ballot change repairs it. Scope asserted: in a two-node configuration where the single dropped Accepted is exactly what the write quorum still needs, the quorum-accepted entry stays undecided for at least 100 resend periods with no repair enabled by the protocol itself, and progress requires a new proposal or a leadership change. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the core API documents no bounded decision time and its resend knob is a recommendation, so the finding rests on the library's own loss-tolerance claim plus this snapshot's intentional message dropping; (b) a client retry (the runtime's documented 'retry safe' Timeout) effectively repairs the earlier entry as a side effect, so the lost duty is bounded by client retry behaviour rather than by the protocol; (c) only a 2-node configuration is probed, where one drop is quorum-critical - in wider clusters the same drop is masked whenever another follower's receipt still completes the quorum, and dropping all needed receipts is a stronger fault assumption; (d) the window is 500 logical steps with an error-free, in-order transport.
limitations: Only the 2-node configuration is probed: the gap bites when the dropped receipt(s) are exactly those the write quorum still needs.

result.summary: Updated the event-backpressure question with the executed consequence case. Receipt 76557a280cf8429d8ce3102d7565decb (experiment 2b18b51118e04d8a9f0ca6001d18eb51-experiment, exit 0, all three tests passed) carries everything in one run: event 2 `parked_majority_cluster` {nodes_parked:2, healthy_node_responsive:true, append_notify_timeout_reached:true, decided_before:7, decided_after:7} — only node 1 consumes its event stream (capacity 8), two of three nodes park, and the healthy node reaches the documented Timeout and cannot move the decided index; events 0/1 are the drained control (all three answering, follower append_notify Ok); events 3/4 restate the node-local freeze (bound reached, permanently parked). interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account of the new question, no execution yet. A follower replies to each AcceptDecide/AcceptStopSign with an Accepted that carries only the receipt's ballot and the follower's accepted_idx (follower.rs:160-175), and the leader turns those receipts into a decision when `is_chosen` sees a quorum of advertised accepted indexes (leader.rs:316-345). Both roles have a periodic callback - SequencePaxos::resend_message_timeout dispatches to resend_messages_leader/resend_messages_follower every resend_message_tick_timeout logical ticks (mod.rs:229-246) - but in the accept phase the leader's version only resends a pending StopSign (or its decide) and re-Prepares peers that are not promised (leader.rs:371-403), and the follower's version is the empty `Phase::Accept => ()` arm (follower.rs:240-269); the follower's other periodic path, flush_batch_follower, replies only when the batch flush itself advanced the accepted index (follower.rs:284-290). So the direction follower->leader has no timer-driven retry, and the leader has no way to ask a follower for its accepted index; the only later trigger is a new AcceptDecide arriving for new entries, which makes the follower advertise a (possibly larger) accepted_idx. Whether that leaves a genuinely quorum-accepted entry undecided for an unbounded interval with no enabled repair under normal (no further proposal) conditions is exactly what the registered discriminator is to decide; no defect is claimed before it runs.
limitations: The claim depends on the environment being permitted to lose a single message while the transport keeps the rest in order; the probe must drop only the Accepted reply and keep delivering everything else.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, corrected by the executed run. The suspicion was that a lost follower Accepted reply is never repaired by any timer-driven or self-initiated action, so a quorum-accepted entry stays undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives (source reading: resend_messages_leader's Accept arm only re-Prepares unpremised peers and resends a pending StopSign; resend_messages_follower's Accept arm is empty; flush_batch_follower replies only when the flush itself advanced the accepted index). Execution 9a8b2864badf41a183a56bcfe91e49a2 (experiment 34c476dd304f48f59580ab2799b029d3-experiment, exit 101) ran the probe and defeats that suspicion in the probed configuration: parsed event 1 `lost_accepted_window` records dropped=Accepted:1, follower_accepted_idx=1, accept_decide_total=1 (so no new client proposal was made in the whole 500-step window) and yet leader_decided_idx=1 with follower_decided_idx=1 - the entry did become decided. The same event names the wire traffic that did it: produced = BLE:676,Prepare:4,Promise:6,AcceptSync:6,AcceptDecide:1,Accepted:3,PrepareReq:2,Decide:1. Three Accepted replies were produced although only one AcceptDecide exists, which matches the accept-sync path in the follower: handle_acceptsync pushes a fresh Accepted carrying the follower's current accepted index (follower.rs:53-79) and it runs whenever the follower is back in Phase::Prepare, i.e. after a new Prepare/Promise cycle (Prepare:4, Promise:6, AcceptSync:6). So the acceptance is re-advertised through ballot-change and re-sync paths rather than through the empty Accept-phase resend arms; the source reading of the empty arms is unchanged, but it does not imply non-repair. Counter-limitation and necessary gap that the correction does not remove: the churn in this run may be an artifact of the previous harness's cadence (it ticked both nodes before draining and delivering anything, which can put a heartbeat reply into a later BLE round than the request that asked for it), so this receipt does not establish whether a lost Accepted is repaired when no ballot change occurs; the revised experiment measures the same window again with per-node tick-and-deliver cadence and with after_drop tracing, which will either show the entry undecided (suspicion survives in the faithful configuration) or name the repairing message.
